bib.title: TensorFlow: A system for large-scale machine learning

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only (no appendices in this paper).

question: How can a single dataflow-graph system support large-scale distributed training and inference on heterogeneous hardware while staying extensible to new optimizers, models and coordination schemes?
hypothesis: A dataflow graph with mutable state subsumes parameter-server designs and lets users build optimizers, sharding, fault tolerance and synchronous replication in user-level code with little overhead.
contributions: A unified dataflow graph with mutable state (variables, queues) covering computation, parameters and input pipelines
User-level extensibility case studies: differentiation/optimizers, very large sharded models, checkpoint fault tolerance, synchronous replication with backup workers
Evaluation of single-machine overhead, synchronous coordination, Inception-v3 and LSTM language-model scaling

method.summary: TensorFlow represents computation and state as one dataflow graph placed across CPUs, GPUs and TPUs, partitioned per device with Send/Recv. Parameter-server behaviour, sharded embeddings, checkpointing and sync/async/backup-worker replication are built from graph primitives. Evaluation measures system throughput and step time, not accuracy.

limits: Measures system throughput and step time only; the authors defer time-to-accuracy and convergence benefits of synchronous replication to other papers.
Evaluated on a shared production cluster, so noise is present; no run counts or seeds given.
Default policies for most users are undetermined; automatic placement, kernel fusion, memory management, scheduling still in development.
Mutable state and fault tolerance suit only weak consistency; checkpoints are not guaranteed consistent.
Static dataflow graph limits dynamic algorithms such as deep RL (conceded in Conclusions).
Dated: parameter server era, K40 GPUs, async SGD; no tensor/pipeline parallelism, mixed precision or collective all-reduce (only noted as under investigation).
